intro: Lesson 17: The Khulafa ar-Rashidun and Abu Bakr as the first caliph. To understand who the Rightly Guided Caliphs were and how Abu Bakr became the first caliph

questions.q: Explain why the Companions chose Abu Bakr.
questions.a: He was the Prophet's ﷺ closest companion, truthful, had led the prayers in the Prophet's ﷺ illness, and was chosen by consultation.
questions.model: Point: Abu Bakr was the most trusted Companion. Evidence: he led the prayers in the Prophet's ﷺ last illness (Bukhari and Muslim). Explain: the Companions consulted and agreed on him. Link: leadership in Islam is a trust.

questions.q: Put in order: Uthman, Abu Bakr, Ali, Umar.

Make a caliph fact file for Abu Bakr on the pupil PDF (title, dates, how chosen, one quality), then write in the portal response box why his speech mattered. Start: 'Abu Bakr's words mattered because ...'
questions.a: Accurate fact file; speech kept Muslims focused on worshipping Allah alone
questions.model: Teacher fills 'Title: as-Siddiq, the truthful' and 'Dates: 632 to 634 CE'.

questions.a: Muhammad ﷺ is a messenger; messengers before him died; Islam continues.

questions.q: why is shura a good way to choose a leader?
questions.a: People discuss, share wisdom and agree together.

questions.q: Back to our ponder: what did the community need, and how did Abu Bakr help?
questions.a: Calm, truth and a trusted leader: he reminded them Allah is alive.
